title: SLO-driven autoscaling runbook for hybrid inference workloads
author: Asha Kumar
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook prescribes SLO-driven autoscaling and emergency mitigation guidance for hybrid inference fleets that serve both real-time (low-latency) and batch (throughput-oriented) LLM workloads. It codifies SLO definitions, error budget gating for scale actions, capacity safety margins, and the operational steps to restore SLOs when violated. The guidance applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private clusters running the Redwood serving runtime.

Scope
-----
- Services: inference-gateway, request-router, model-worker-pool, cache-proxy
- Workloads: conversational low-latency (p95-sensitive), bulk-embedding jobs (throughput-sensitive), reranking pipelines (mixed)
- Environments: prod, prod-canary, staging

Goals
-----
1) Keep p95 latency for real-time requests <= 250 ms for "tier-1" customers (SLO A).
2) Maintain request success rate >= 99.95% (SLO B).
3) Keep batch queue lag < 30s median and < 120s 99th percentile for embeddings jobs (SLO C).
4) Use error budget burn to guide cross-region/fallback routing and temporary capacity bursts.

SLO and error budget definitions
-------------------------------
- SLO A (real-time latency): p95 <= 250 ms, measured at proxy edge excluding throttled requests. Window: 30 days. Allocation: 99.9%
- SLO B (availability): request success rate >= 99.95% over 30 days. Failure = 5xx, 4xx-customer-throttled, or internal-circuit-breaker responses.
- SLO C (batch lag): median queue lag < 30s, p99 < 120s over 7 days.

Error budget math (example)
- For SLO A (30d window): allowable p95 exceedance = 0.1% of request-hours; operationalized as 43.2 minutes of equivalent outage over 30d.

Capacity assumptions and safety margins
-------------------------------------
- Model-worker instance profile: gpu-v100-32 with baseline throughput of 20 tokens/s for model-family-x, 60 tokens/s for quantized-family-q per replica.
- Autoscaler target: keep GPU utilization across model-worker-pool <= 70% for burst safety.
- Safety reserve: maintain at least N+2 replicas above predicted baseline for prod (N = expected replicas for 99th percentile load).

Traffic characterization and tagging
----------------------------------
- Tag requests at ingress: {customer_tier, intent=real_time|batch|rerank, model_size}. Use these tags in Prometheus labels for SLO and scaling queries.

Autoscaling policy (high-level)
------------------------------
1) Horizontal scaling for model-worker-pool driven by grouped metrics: real_time_qps, batch_queue_depth, avg_kv_cache_hit_rate.
2) Prefer elastic burst capacity (pre-warmed pooled instances) for sudden spikes under error budget.
3) If error budget > 50% remaining: allow opportunistic scale-out to reduce latency and preemptively migrate batch to spare capacity.
4) If error budget < 20% remaining: restrict non-critical batch jobs, enable conservative per-tenant throttling, and avoid large preemptive scale-outs.

Prometheus alerting and query patterns
-------------------------------------
- Example queries (PromQL):
  - Real-time p95 latency (edge): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - Model-worker GPU utilization: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[5m]) by (instance_group)
  - Batch queue depth: sum(inference_queue_length) by (queue_name)
  - Error budget burn rate (30d window): (1 - request_success_ratio_30d) / (1 - SLO_target)

Alert thresholds (examples)
- P1: real-time p95 > 300ms for 5m and rising -> page SRE on-call, run emergency mitigation.
- P1: request success rate drops below 99.8% for 10m -> page SRE and Platform Eng.
- P2: batch p99 queue lag > 180s for 15m -> notify platform team, consider throttling elective batch.

Automated actions vs manual runbook steps
----------------------------------------
- Automated (safe, reversible): horizontal scale-out by one replica, enable pre-warmed burst pool, route to secondary region when configured. These actions require error budget gating per policy above.
- Manual (require SRE approval or paging): force model fallback to smaller quantized family, perform global rebalancing, evacuate noisy tenant.

Operational run steps: SLO breach (real-time p95)
------------------------------------------------
1) Triage and confirm: check Grafana dashboard "SLO: real-time latency" and confirm p95 > 300ms sustained for 5m.
2) Check recent deploys: gitops change list: git log --since="1 hour" origin/main -- services/inference-gateway
3) Inspect edge and worker metrics:
   - kubectl -n prod get hpa -l app=model-worker-pool -o wide
   - curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))" | jq .data.result
4) If GPU utilization < 70% and queue depth rising: trigger autoscaler to add 1 replica: kubectl -n prod patch hpa model-worker-pool --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":10}]' (adjust to target).
5) If GPU utilization > 85%: route traffic to fallback model variant per routing policy: use the request-router admin API POST /admin/route/fallback {"model_family":"q-family","percent":30}
6) If error budget < 20%: do NOT perform large preemptive scale-outs. Instead, enable tenant-level throttles and short-lived tail latency mitigations (percentile-limited shed).
7) Post-mitigation: monitor 15m window. If SLO recovers, begin gradual rollback of emergency actions after 30m of stable metrics.

Operational run steps: batch backlog surge
---------------------------------------
1) Detect: batch queue depth > surge_threshold (configurable per queue).
2) If error budget available (> 40%): opportunistically spin up pre-warmed batch workers in burst pool. CLI: rhctl capacity allocate --pool=batch-burst --count 5 --reason "batch surge"
3) If error budget low: prioritize critical tenants, pause non-critical scheduling: POST /scheduler/pause?label=best-effort
4) Avoid moving batch to real-time worker pool unless explicitly approved due to cache interference; prefer isolated batch workers.

Emergency fallbacks and smoke tests
----------------------------------
- Global fallback: if primary region capacity exhausted and error budget > 10%, failover to secondary region using routing policy: request-router sets route_weight(primary)=0.6, secondary=0.4.
- Smoke test sequence after failover:
  1) curl -X POST https://api-redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke test","max_tokens":4}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY'
  2) Check p95 on smoke endpoint.
  3) Validate KV cache hit-rate and cold-start counts in last 15m.

Incident review and RCA standards (short form)
-------------------------------------------
- Capture timeline with at least 1-minute granularity for the incident window (start -> mitigations -> recovery). Use telemetry export: /scripts/export_incident_window.sh --start "2026-02-10T12:00Z" --end "2026-02-10T13:30Z"
- Required RCA sections: problem statement, impact quantification (errors, latency, cost), hypothesis, experiments run, root cause, corrective actions, owners, target completion dates.
- Use the standard template: RCA must include a quantitative regression test and a post-deployment canary plan.

Operational tooling & dashboards
------------------------------
- Dashboards to have:
  - SLO Overview (p95, success rate, error budget remaining)
  - Node & GPU capacity (utilization, pre-warmed pool status)
  - Queue health (per-queue depth, enqueued age distribution)
  - Tenant hot-path heatmap (top 10 tenants by QPS / latency contribution)
- Playbook integrations: Slack alerting channel #sre-alerts, automatic Jira ticket creation for P1s with tags [incident, autoscale].

Testing and rehearsals
---------------------
- Monthly chaos exercises: simulate cold-cache bursts, sudden +3x sustained QPS, and model-worker node loss. Record outcomes and update safety margins.
- Runbook drills: on-call SRE runs the mitigation steps in staging with a 10m bounded ramp every quarter.

Change gating and rollout guidance
---------------------------------
- Any change to autoscaler thresholds or safety reserve requires: a) performance bench with representative prompts, b) a canary rollout (5% traffic for 2h), and c) error budget check (>= 60% remaining) before full rollout.

Owners and maintenance cadence
----------------------------
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (oncall rotation: platform-sre@redwood.com)
- Secondary owner: Runtime team (runtime-oncall@redwood.com)
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly; tabletop drills annually.

Appendix: sample HPA YAML snippet (for reference)
------------------------------------------------
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-worker-pool
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: model-worker-deployment
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 40
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: gpu_utilization_percent
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "70"

Contacts and escalation
-----------------------
- P1: page #oncall-sre (30m SLA to acknowledge). If not acknowledged, escalate to SRE manager.
- P2: notify Slack thread and create a Jira ops ticket.
